results.title: Want a Sustainable Phone? The Modular Fairphone 6 Could Be the Answer - CNET
results.content:
While this is technically the Fairphone 6, the company wants it to be known as just the Fairphone — the thinking being that you shouldn’t need to upgrade your phone every few years to the next generation of devices. Fairphone promises seven Android updates and support for software and repairable parts through 2033 with this device.

That said, this is only case if you buy the phone in Europe. In the US, it will only ship (initally at least) running e/OS — a privacy- and ethics-focused operating system made by French company Murena, which will also serve as US distributor. [...] The Fairphone 6, aka “the Fairphone.”

Katie Collins/CNET

Sustainable tech leader Fairphone unveiled its latest modular device on Thursday at an event in Amsterdam, presenting a clear challenge to mainstream phone-makers everywhere. The Fairphone 6 is a fully repairable phone built to last, with what the company says is its lowest carbon footprint yet. [...] Fairphone’s big sell is its longevity, but that doesn’t mean it wants to compromise on user experience. Its previous phone, the Fairphone 5, scored 7/10 in our review. But it also earned a 10/10 teardown score from iFixit. iFixit is a leader in providing the tools and knowledge for people to repair their electronics and has been at the forefront of pushing right-to-repair legislation.

img-7646

The Fairphone comes with Google services — but only in Europe.

Katie Collins/CNET

The Fairphone is entirely modular, with replaceable elements that make it both easy to fix and more fun. You can replace the battery, screen, camera, ports and other components — and snap off the rear cover to attach accessories like a carry cord or card holder.

results.title: Longevity Fairphone - Improving smartphone longevity
results.content:
# Longevity

We design long-lasting products that are built to last. Because the longer you keep your phone, the smaller the environmental impact. Our hardware is durable and dependable, with our signature modular design making it easy to swap parts like the display and the battery when needed. When it comes to warranty periods and after sales support, we’re breaking industry conventions and records, offering longer support windows than anyone else.

## Why do things need to change?

### We’re fighting against a market trend where the average phone is replaced way too early and too often. That’s not good for anyone in the long run. [...] 2024: We released the Fairbuds, our first repairable wireless earbuds that scored a perfect 10/10 iFixit score.
 2023: The Fairphone 5 becomes one of the first phones to launch with an IoT chipset that allows software support for at least eight years.
 2021: The Fairphone 4 becomes the first to offer a 5-year extended manufacturer warranty. It was also our first 5G smartphone.
 2020: We released a physical camera hardware upgrade for the Fairphone 3, which had launched a year prior. Users could easily make the upgrade themselves, thanks to its robust modular design. [...] ## Hardware that endures

Our devices are designed to last. We make it easy for our customers to keep using their phones for a very long time. How do we do this? Our modular design makes swapping parts easy. Pop in a spare battery or replace the display in minutes. Our spare parts are more than affordable compared to the competition, and will be available for years to come on our webshop. Instructions on making quick and easy DIY repairs can be found on our website as well. In case you do need professional repairs, we are more than happy to help. We also constantly share maintenance tips and other advice with the Fairphone community to extend your device’s life.

results.content:
most repairable smartphone of 2025, and that has got to go to the Fairphone 6. Fairphone only 
releases one phone every two or three years, which is a reasonable schedule. It's a 
totally modular smartphone where every component is held in place with screws; no 
heat required to melt or soften adhesive. It is a bit pricey and replacement parts are 
hard to source in the USA, but overseas the Fairphone 6 makes a lot of sense since it's 
designed from the ground up to be future-proof, upgradable, and repairable. I wish Fairphone 
were more mainstream, but alas, it is not. If I were, however, to pick one of 
the main players—you know, Samsung, Apple, or Google—and pick which of their 
phones of theirs are the most repairable, I would have to give a shout-out to Google. [...] phone for a special group of people. If I had to pick the least durable smartphone of 2025, it’s 
got to go to the Pixel 10 Fold. Normally, I'd give folding phones a pass for breaking, but Samsung's 
normal folding phones didn't break. Google's folding phones, have all broken in the same spot 
for three years in a row, and this year’s even exploded. That is not ideal, and it's time to 
call them out. For sure, if you treat your phone nicely, it's probably not going to break. But 
as a manufacturer if Google knows there's a weak spot in their design and they don't address it, 
that's a big deal because some of us care about durability. So, congrats to the Pixel 10 Pro Fold
